reading_rule: Complete selected scientific source values, with custody-only fields removed as documented. Author-state tokens remain dated source history; original later qualification governs scientific acceptance.

mapping_contract.native_fields_preserved: All 40 complete native property records in LEAN_REQUALIFIED_LEDGER.json; exact field changes listed separately
mapping_contract.proposition: MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM interpreted with TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT, DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS and REQUALIFICATION ceiling
mapping_contract.authority: IMPROVEMENT_AUTHORITY plus the selected scoped authority model
mapping_contract.criticism: IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS and KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES, linked criticism ledger
mapping_contract.loss_warning: No historical executable predicate, numeric confidence or independent-study count inferred from qualitative native fields

claims.bearer: A decision about an output or intervention and its affected beneficiaries
claims.scientific_origin: Normative/analytical outcome framing informed by Lean value doctrine
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S010/S011 and R008 establish doctrine; heterogeneous domain findings do not prove that a value-statement format causes benefit. S060 is narrowed by R005.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Time to identify affected parties and observe outcomes; expensive measurement can exceed trivial work's value.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: State whose outcome is sought and which constraints cannot be traded away; leave effects unknown when only throughput is measured.

claims.bearer: A bounded work path from demand to beneficiary outcome
claims.scientific_origin: Historical flow concepts plus analytical end-to-end extension
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S003/S005 describe replenishment and flow; a map is a representation, not proof of lower total delay. Current software telemetry is a domain analogy.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Observation and maintaining boundary definitions; possible surveillance and stale models.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Include waiting before entry, rework and downstream delay when comparing local cycle times.

claims.bearer: A work-state representation and an intended human responder
claims.scientific_origin: Historical visual control with contemporary representation analogy
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S005 supports andon history. S066's small review cannot prove all labeling, boards or telemetry effective.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Updating displays and responder attention, privacy and access burden.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: State must be current, interpretable and actionable for the specified decision; a label alone is insufficient.

claims.bearer: A release/admission rule over a defined class of work items
claims.scientific_origin: Historical kanban; Hopp/Spearman tactical pull interpretation; software translation
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S006 includes stock, planning and conditional kanban quantities. S032 defines explicit WIP control; S056's correlations do not identify an optimal software limit.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Admission delay, starvation risk and exception handling.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: A limit genuinely bounds the declared in-process population; total waiting and service risk remain separate outcomes.
claims.precondition_scope: Release/WIP control governs active commitments. A reduction in one admitted or deployed population need not improve total waiting, value or safety; a coherent broader configuration is not necessary for every narrowly defined partial effect.

claims.bearer: A batch and its setup, processing, validation and feedback economics
claims.scientific_origin: Manufacturing mechanism with explicit analytical transfer
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S006/S032 support setup-capacity trade-offs; numerical examples test economics, not universal human-work performance. S057 is not freshly read.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Repeated setup and validation versus delay, inventory and failure exposure.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Compare total cost and feedback time at a coherent work unit; a smaller batch need not be cheaper.
claims.precondition_scope: Validation and recovery support qualified or reversible delivery claims. They are not necessary for every partial reduction in the affected population when an enforced smaller deployment is isolated; batch cost, lost benefit and overall risk remain separate.

claims.bearer: A transition between work types or released versions
claims.scientific_origin: Historical setup reduction; analogy to software-native automation
claims.current_evidence_warrant: Toyota chronology and S032 support setup logic. Modern pipelines are not proved to descend directly from die-change methods.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Automation, preparation, maintenance and recovery effort.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Reduce total safe transition cost; include work shifted to preparation or other teams.

claims.bearer: A capacity plan for a measurable demand class
claims.scientific_origin: TPS pacing and later contingent HMLV adaptation
claims.current_evidence_warrant: Corrected S063 supplies a particular procedure; S064 reports theoretical gaps. No fixed takt is inferred for novel discovery tasks.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Forecasting, schedule changes and buffers against remaining variation.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Apply a stable cadence only to the predictable component and review its workload consequences.

claims.bearer: A system's portfolio of physical buffers and resilience-enabling options
claims.scientific_origin: Operations-science model plus analytical and supply-chain interpretation
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S032 distinguishes inventory, capacity and time. Information and alternate designs may improve decisions or future capacity; they are not interchangeable physical stock. R002/R009 are corporate description/proposal.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Carrying cost, spare capacity, time delay, information upkeep and dormant alternatives.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Name the variability and consequence absorbed by each reserve; reject any claimed substitution that lacks a feasible material/recovery path.

claims.bearer: A loading policy for a service or production system
claims.scientific_origin: Queueing/flow reasoning, not a universal anti-utilization rule
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S032's conditional arguments support capacity/WIP attention. Deterministic balanced service can be fully utilized without queuing; stochastic overload cannot be cured by a board.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Reserve capacity and foregone short-run output.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Evaluate throughput, waiting, variability and recovery jointly; do not infer harm from a utilization number alone.

claims.bearer: A demand or replenishment signal consumed by a release decision
claims.scientific_origin: Historical kanban plus analytical information contract
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S006 combines short-term withdrawal with advance production planning. Current electronic signal forms are implementation alternatives.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Reconciliation, signal maintenance and forecast-error monitoring.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Check origin, units, freshness and decision scope; actual withdrawals alone do not establish long-lead capacity.

claims.bearer: A detector and signal path for a specified abnormal condition
claims.scientific_origin: Documented jidoka/andon history; analytical modern detection analogy
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S001/S005/S067 establish doctrine and history; S031/R001 show that involvement does not prevent ergonomic failures. Detector performance requires its own evidence.
claims.incremental_control_cost: False alarms, missed defects, attention and instrumentation.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Separate detection, transmission, acknowledgement and response; demonstrate each required link at its scope.

claims.bearer: A containment/stop decision and its authorized responders
claims.scientific_origin: Historical worker/line response with bounded analytical extension
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S006 documents worker stop participation. The current severity/authority design is proposed; feature flags and circuit breakers are analogues unless influence is documented.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Lost output, safe-state transitions, investigation and recovery capacity.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Consequence, propagation and authority determine the smallest safe containment; stopping is neither diagnosis nor durable prevention.

claims.bearer: Output creation and the checks or containment before release
claims.scientific_origin: Historical quality-at-source with software-domain convergence
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S001/S005/S010 support source quality logic. Local checks cannot establish unseen interface or system-level properties.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Inspection, validation delays and missed-mode risk.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Test the relevant failure before propagation when feasible, preserving additional system assurance where local scope is insufficient.

claims.bearer: A stable error opportunity and a constraint against it
claims.scientific_origin: Mistake-proofing mechanism; analogy to modern types/interlocks
claims.current_evidence_warrant: Historical examples support defect prevention. Type systems and safe defaults are not established here as descendants of Toyota jigs.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Constraint design, bypass/recovery provisions and maintenance.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: The constraint addresses an identified error class without creating worse new failures; an unmodelled hazard remains open.

claims.bearer: An automation/human exception arrangement
claims.scientific_origin: Jidoka history plus explicit modern automation analogy
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S001/S067 support automatic abnormality stoppage. Human-on-the-loop effectiveness is not established by those historical examples.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Human training and readiness, handoff load, automation maintenance.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Bound the routine task and abnormal handoff; show competent response is available, rather than assuming human presence guarantees recovery.

claims.bearer: A measurement and variation analysis for a defined process
claims.scientific_origin: Documented statistical-quality import and separate statistical reasoning
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S010/S011 support institutional adoption; they do not prove that any chosen chart is valid or that stable output meets user needs.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Sampling, measurement assurance and analytical expertise.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Specify data and assumptions; separate stability, capability and acceptability. No theorem is asserted from a chart label.

claims.bearer: A scoped current method and its legitimate revision
claims.scientific_origin: Historical standard work with authored lifecycle safeguards
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S004/S008/S009 support training/baseline history. Explicit expiry and retirement are analytical safeguards, not universal historical TPS requirements; S026/S031 expose coercion risks.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Document maintenance, training and delayed change decisions.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Preserve enough baseline to compare performance while allowing justified exceptions and proportionate changes.

claims.bearer: An inquiry into actual work using observation and other evidence
claims.scientific_origin: Genchi/genbutsu-related practice with analytical triangulation
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S068's locator failed. S031/R001 and S026 independently show why worker testimony and records can challenge managerial descriptions.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Observation, consent/privacy, trace collection and interpretation time.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Use observations for what they reveal, distinguish inference, and add evidence for latent or distributed causes.

claims.bearer: A proposed countermeasure to a defined problem
claims.scientific_origin: Quality/problem-solving traditions plus analytical causal discrimination
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S046/S047/S048 support concern about ritual and weak inquiry; S047 does not show that reported PDSA fidelity causes success. A3/Five Whys names confer no evidential force.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Investigation, safe testing, alternatives and follow-up.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: A prediction is compared with observed results and competing explanations at proportionate scope; a valid result may be no change.

claims.bearer: An adopted improvement and its ongoing benefit/burden
claims.scientific_origin: Analytical lifecycle extension informed by sustainment research
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S043/S044 are bounded event evidence; fixed universal expiry periods are not established. Retirement may depend on changed conditions instead of a calendar.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Monitoring and maintaining controls can consume the benefit they protect.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Use a trigger or review proportionate to change/risk; retain, revise or retire from evidence without a mandatory paperwork cycle.

claims.bearer: Worker capabilities and cross-coverage for material tasks
claims.scientific_origin: TWI/TPS training history and socio-technical candidate
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S008/S009 establish selective training influence with conflicting exact dates. S031 and R003 do not establish that training alone improves wellbeing.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Protected training, coaching, staffing and skill preservation.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Check demonstrated competence and workload effects; training completion does not establish authority or spare response capacity.

claims.bearer: A worker's ability to report, receive response and exercise bounded rights
claims.scientific_origin: Normative socio-technical safeguard, historically and empirically informed
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S026/S031/S070 distinguish experience from doctrine. R004's strain/safety associations are mixed and cannot justify overload or negate adverse longitudinal findings.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Response staffing, protected time, appeals and bargaining/representation arrangements.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Distinguish voice, acknowledgement, action rights and retaliation protection; recorded suggestions alone establish none of the latter.

claims.bearer: The employment and distributional terms surrounding improvement
claims.scientific_origin: Contextual institutional history plus normative fair-transition proposal
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S013/S014 describe conflict and agreement; S026/S031 show divergent outcomes. No universally necessary no-layoff policy or measured causal guarantee is inferred.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Employment guarantees, redeployment, negotiation and sharing gains.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Identify who gains, loses or carries risk and whether commitments are credible; do not turn doctrine into an observed worker outcome.

claims.bearer: Management decisions controlling resources, incentives and cross-boundary causes
claims.scientific_origin: Historical response roles with analytical responsibility allocation
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S005 documents supervisory practice; S046 shows that local investigators may lack system authority. Associations in S027/S030 do not prove every governance design effective.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Management attention, escalation capacity and opportunity costs.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Assign problems to actors able to change the relevant condition; do not blame an operator for unavailable structural authority.

claims.bearer: A measurement regime used to make system decisions
claims.scientific_origin: Analytical proxy governance; historical and modern metric critique
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S011 records removal of suggestion-count targets. Current S058 is guidance and S059 a framework; neither metric conformity nor balanced dashboards prove beneficiary value.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Data maintenance, countermetrics, privacy and gaming audits.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Keep denominators and boundaries stable enough for comparison; examine transferred harm and the intended outcome.

claims.bearer: A physical asset or software service's maintenance/recovery policy
claims.scientific_origin: TPS equipment reliability plus modern reliability convergence
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S005 supports equipment reliability context; S041/S042 provide observational manufacturing associations. Error budgets are contemporary analogues, not proven direct TPS descendants.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Maintenance labor, spares, downtime and recovery exercises.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Choose policy for the asset's failure/recovery consequences; low-cost replacement may be adequate for a noncritical item.
claims.precondition_scope: Maintenance and recovery address their named reliability/restore functions. Lack of recovery does not negate a separately demonstrated reduction in the number of independent instances exposed to a fault.

claims.bearer: A buyer–supplier or dependency capability relationship
claims.scientific_origin: Historical supplier institutions plus normative allocation safeguards
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S069/S038 describe capability and knowledge mechanisms. Neither establishes fair distribution; fairness is an explicit selected criterion, not a reported universal fact.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Joint training, disclosure, negotiation and dependence/lock-in.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Joint gain must account for supplier viability and shifted costs, rather than only buyer inventory or price.

claims.bearer: Critical multilevel dependencies and feasible recovery options
claims.scientific_origin: Corporate disruption history and author design proposals
claims.current_evidence_warrant: R002 reports item information; R009 proposes virtual dualization. The inherited HIGH_POST_DISRUPTION_DOMAIN label is not evidence of a causal efficacy estimate.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Mapping, confidentiality, data freshness and qualifying alternatives.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Map only where it changes buffer/recovery choices; known dependency without a feasible action does not establish resilience.

claims.bearer: A design decision with uncertain coupled constraints and costly reversal
claims.scientific_origin: Product-development case interpretation and option-value analysis
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S050/S052 support set-based concepts; S049 full monograph is not freshly read. Comparative causal superiority remains open.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Parallel analysis, prototype cost, coordination and delayed commitment.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Retain alternatives only while expected learning/avoided reversal justifies cost; eliminate from evidence and respect delivery deadlines.

claims.bearer: Cross-disciplinary decisions and reusable design trade-off knowledge
claims.scientific_origin: Automotive development interpretation; contemporary implementations are analogies
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S049's comparative details remain inherited; S050/S052 support integration concepts. Digital-thread or model-based descent is not established.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Interface maintenance, coordination and meeting opportunity costs.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Bring affected disciplines to consequential interfaces; a small independent decision does not need universal participation.

claims.bearer: A software service's flow, qualification and recovery configuration
claims.scientific_origin: Practitioner Lean/Kanban translation and convergence with software engineering
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S053 documents translation; S056 offers WIP correlations; S058 current guidance and S059 framework are not independent causal tests of the full bundle. S057 full text is not freshly read.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Automation, test/monitor maintenance, on-call load and rollback capability.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Select controls for service risk and actual change bottlenecks; a board or deployment count is insufficient, and a tiny safe change may use fewer controls.
claims.precondition_scope: The listed preconditions concern the fuller selected sustainable-delivery configuration. They are not jointly necessary for every partial release-scope effect, and their presence is not sufficient for overall benefit.

claims.bearer: A portfolio admission, continuation or retirement decision
claims.scientific_origin: Analytical extension from value and commitment limits
claims.current_evidence_warrant: R008/S053 provide conceptual ancestry; the specific stop/retire rule is a normative proposal, not an established Lean efficacy result.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Evaluation, transition, lost options and switching costs.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Compare continuation with alternatives and transition costs; cheap completion may dominate an elaborate cancellation process.

claims.bearer: The universal rule to eliminate every item labelled waste
claims.scientific_origin: Rejected universal; replaced by explicit conditional mechanisms
claims.current_evidence_warrant: A buffer or control can have protective value even if it consumes resources. This defeats a universal rule, not every concrete waste reduction.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Overcorrection can remove useful reserves or turn analysis into new ceremony.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Ask what protective or learning function is lost before removal; no claim that all waste terminology is useless.

claims.bearer: The universal instruction to minimize or eliminate all inventory
claims.scientific_origin: Rejected universal with surviving conditional inventory reduction
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S006/S067 explicitly accommodate stock and S032 models buffering. Physical shortages provide a counterexample; this does not establish stockpiling as optimal.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Carrying cost and obsolescence remain real alternatives to shortage risk.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Reject only unqualified minimization; a stable fast-replenished item may legitimately need little stock.

claims.bearer: The universal objective of maximum utilization and zero slack
claims.scientific_origin: Rejected universal with deterministic boundary control
claims.current_evidence_warrant: Variable arrivals and repair needs undermine universal full loading. C02 also preserves a fully utilized deterministic case without queueing.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Spare capacity costs money and may be unnecessary in a stable bounded task.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Determine variability and service consequences; neither maximum nor deliberately low utilization is universally correct.

claims.bearer: The universal instruction to use the smallest possible batch
claims.scientific_origin: Rejected universal with small-batch positive control
claims.current_evidence_warrant: Setup costs can outweigh reduced delay; lowering setup can reverse the preferred batch. This is an economic counterexample, not a field effect estimate.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Setup, validation and coherence costs versus feedback delay.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Compare feasible batches and costs; retain single-piece flow when the relevant setup and risks permit it.

claims.bearer: Method-name or artifact-format conformity as a universal quality condition
claims.scientific_origin: Ceremony rejected; implementation choices remain available
claims.current_evidence_warrant: A board, A3 sheet or named method is neither necessary nor sufficient for the underlying mechanism. Native use may still be convenient.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Artifact production, training and compliance burden.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Accept a simpler mechanism that achieves the required local decision; do not reject tools merely because they are branded.

claims.bearer: Activity volume as proof of improvement
claims.scientific_origin: Rejected evidentiary implication
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S011 documents count-target withdrawal; S047 shows reported method deficiencies without an efficacy comparison. More completed events cannot by itself prove better outcomes.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Gaming, time spent producing counts and suppression of inconvenient evidence.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Require outcome/learning evidence for the claim made; counts can still describe workload without proving improvement.

claims.bearer: Universal synchronization, concentration or single sourcing
claims.scientific_origin: Rejected universal with contingent supplier arrangements preserved
claims.current_evidence_warrant: Disruption descriptions and R009 proposals motivate scrutiny; they do not prove that diversification always improves resilience or that integration is inherently harmful.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Duplicated qualification, lost scale and common-cause alternatives.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Compare concentration, alternatives and recovery by criticality; a qualified single source with adequate protection may be justified.

claims.bearer: Immutable procedure compliance as universal correctness
claims.scientific_origin: Rejected universal; stable safety constraints remain legitimate
claims.current_evidence_warrant: S026/S031 challenge coercive practice; legitimate exceptions and changed conditions defeat immutability. Stable constraints may remain unchanged when still valid.
claims.incremental_control_cost: Revision and coordination burdens can exceed a tiny reversible task.
claims.qualitative_evaluation_criterion: Permit justified deviation/change at proper authority while preserving still-valid constraints; compliance alone is not an outcome.
